macros.name: By
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto, and \Error.

macros.name: const
macros.doc: We typeset constants like NIL, TRUE, and RED in small caps with the \const command, e.g., \const{nil}, \const{true}, and \const{red}.

macros.name: Do
macros.doc: \Do produces the keyword do, and it also increments the indentation level.

macros.name: Downto
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto, and \Error.

macros.name: ElseIf
macros.doc: For an if-ladder, use \Then for the first case, \ElseNoIf for the last case, and \ElseIf for all intermediate cases.

macros.name: ElseNoIf
macros.doc: For an if-ladder, use \Then for the first case, \ElseNoIf for the last case, and \ElseIf for all intermediate cases.

macros.name: Error
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto, and \Error.

macros.name: For
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto, and \Error.

macros.name: func
macros.doc: We typeset the names of fixed functions in plain old roman with the \func command, e.g., level and out-degree.

macros.name: Goto
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto, and \Error.

macros.name: If
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto, and \Error.

macros.name: proc
macros.doc: For procedure names, use the \proc command. It typesets procedure names in small caps, and dashes (which occur frequently in our procedure names) are typeset as hyphens.

macros.name: Procname
macros.doc: The \Procname command specifies the name of the procedure.

macros.name: RComment
macros.doc: \RComment produces a comment that is flush against the right margin.

macros.name: Return
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto, and \Error.

macros.name: Then
macros.doc: For an if-ladder, use \Then for the first case, \ElseNoIf for the last case, and \ElseIf for all intermediate cases.

macros.name: To
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto, and \Error.

macros.name: twodots
macros.doc: We denote subarrays with the “. .” notation, which is produced by the \twodots command.

macros.name: While
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto, and \Error.

macros.name: zi
macros.doc: To start a new, unnumbered line, use the \zi command.

envs.name: codebox
envs.doc: We typeset pseudocode by putting it in a codebox environment.
